acceptanceCriteria: Reproduce or bound the Linux race in which groupreap reads /proc/<pid>/status for a member of the owned group and finds no Threads line, so quiescence is reported unproved after a clean exit.
Treat a member that exits or becomes a zombie during the /proc quiet proof as quiescent or re-probe it, without accepting real residue; keep refusal when residue exists.
TestRunProcessReapsDescendantBeforeDelayedSideEffect passes repeatedly on Linux CI (for example -count=50) with focused procgroup tests and independent review.
body: Suspected flaky test, observed once in CI on beamfall/corvint#808 (run 38178767381, job 114586863420, go-product-shard (3), ubuntu, go1.27.2, head a8c05c4f45a8971665ee97d2eada7c739a0e0d14). internal/procgroup was not changed by that PR. Actual: TestRunProcessReapsDescendantBeforeDelayedSideEffect (process_test.go:129) failed after 1.01s with Err process-cleanup-failed: prove owned process group quiescence: owned process group quiescence unproved: groupreap: /proc quiet proof unavailable: no thread count for 66079; ExitStatus 0, WaitCompleted true, PipesDrained true, DescendantCleanupStatus owned-process-group. Expected: a descendant that has already exited (or is exiting) is proved quiescent, or the probe retries, so the test passes. Hypothesis (inference): the /proc/<pid>/status read races with the process exiting, so the Threads field is missing. Not reproduced locally (Darwin host has no /proc). Distinct from V1-1055 (signal-0 probe after pgid reuse).
title: procgroup /proc quiet proof fails with no thread count for an exiting group member (CI flake)
